title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Anne Elliot once let herself be persuaded to give up the man she loved. Eight years later, Captain Wentworth returns, rich, proud and still hurt. Jane Austen's gentlest love story asks whether a second chance can ever be as sweet as the first.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Emma Woodhouse is clever, rich and sure that she knows everyone's heart better than they do. Her matchmaking in the little town of Highbury causes tears, quarrels and some very red faces. Only one honest friend can show her what she has been missing.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
blurb: When their father dies, Elinor and Marianne Dashwood lose their home and most of their money. One sister hides her feelings, and the other shows every one. Two broken hearts, one cruel secret and a very long, wet walk will teach them what sense and sensibility are worth.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
blurb: A poor orphan with a fierce heart grows up to be a governess at Thornfield Hall. There she meets its secretive master, Mr Rochester, and learns that love and honesty can pull a person in opposite directions. Will Jane find a home she can keep?

title: North and South
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
blurb: Margaret Hale leaves the green villages of southern England for the smoky mill town of Milton, where she clashes with proud mill owner John Thornton. Strikes, secrets and sorrow force both to question what they believe. Can north and south ever understand each other?

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L. M. Montgomery
blurb: Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert ask for a boy to help on their farm, and a talkative, red-haired girl arrives instead. Anne Shirley fills Green Gables with imagination, mistakes and love. Will the lonely orphan finally find a home, a best friend and a place to belong?

title: Far from the Madding Crowd
author: Thomas Hardy
blurb: A proud, clever young woman inherits a farm and refuses to be ruled by any man. Three very different men love her: a loyal shepherd, a lonely landowner and a dashing soldier. Who will she choose, and what will it cost her?

title: The Age of Innocence
author: Edith Wharton
blurb: In the glittering, rule-bound New York of the 1870s, a young lawyer is about to marry the perfect bride when her mysterious cousin walks into the opera. Newland Archer must choose between duty and desire, and between two women who see him very differently.

title: Cyrano de Bergerac
author: Edmond Rostand
blurb: Cyrano can fight a hundred men and rhyme at the same time, but he believes no woman could love his enormous nose. When the beautiful Roxane falls for a handsome soldier who cannot speak, Cyrano lends him his words, and his own heart.

title: The Rival at Desk Four
author: The Hating Game
blurb: Ines Marlow loves her desk by the window at the Harbourgate Tram Company, until Jonah Pike takes the desk opposite. One job, eight weeks and one stubborn rival. Can two people who must win ever learn to share the road?

title: Just Pretending
author: The Love Hypothesis
blurb: Wren Ashby only wanted her aunt to stop finding her dates. So she said she was already seeing someone, and the nearest man in the café was Kit Navarro. Six weeks, one napkin of rules and one big lantern fair. What could go wrong?

title: Two Keys, One Door
author: The Flatshare
blurb: A letting agent gave the same flat to two strangers on the same day. Odile has a violin and a secret. Sam has headphones and a deadline. One month, one strip of tape down the hall, and two keys to one door.

title: Summer at Willow Bay
author: People We Meet on Vacation
blurb: Nora Bell comes to Willow Bay only to sell her late aunt's boat hut. Then come the dawn rowing lessons, a grumpy boat builder next door and one foggy night on an island. Can one summer change where she belongs?

title: The Runaway Prince
author: Red, White & Royal Blue
blurb: Prince Felix is days from an arranged engagement, so he catches a night train and vanishes. In a lakeside bookshop he becomes plain Fen, a terrible shop assistant, until a festival of lanterns and a newspaper change everything.

title: Letters I Never Sent
author: The Notebook
blurb: Inside a hidden drawer, furniture restorer Iris finds thirty letters that were written but never sent. To deliver them at last, she must travel to a seaside town, and face the letters she has never sent herself.

title: Every July
author: One Day
blurb: One promise made on a jetty at nineteen: meet here every July. Nell and Sam keep it through distance, other people and one missed summer. Will the lanterns on Lake Verna finally light the way home?

title: The Duke's Convenient Bride
author: The Duke and I
blurb: A duke must marry within a year or lose his lands. A clever farmer's daughter needs money to save her family. A contract, a year, three rules. Nobody agreed that it would turn into love.

title: Snowed In at Cedar Lodge
author: The Unhoneymooners
blurb: A secret inspector. A run-down mountain lodge. A snowstorm that closes the only road. Poppy came to judge Cedar Lodge, but four days of burnt soup, bursting pipes and Cal's smile may change what she writes.

title: The Grumpy Baker of Maple Street
author: Book Lovers
blurb: Hazel Quinn comes to Maple Street for one month to fix a baker's books. Jonas Reed is grumpy, proud and up at three every morning. Can a cheerful stranger save his bakery, and can he save her heart?

title: A Wedding to Survive
author: The Wedding Date
blurb: Lena Costa has a three-page list and one job: make her best friend's wedding perfect. Then come a storm, a runaway cake, a very bad dog and the best man, Theo Hart. Some things cannot be planned.

title: The Love Letter Café
author: P.S. I Love You
blurb: Nina Alvarez comes to Marlow Bay to sell her late grandmother's café. Instead she finds twelve secret letters that must be delivered, a town full of unsaid words and Eli, the postman she once left behind.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: A dead man in an empty house, and one word written in blood on the wall. Dr Watson meets Sherlock Holmes and watches him read the clues that no one else can see. But the real story starts far away, years earlier, in a desert.

title: The Sign of the Four
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: A lady with a mystery: her father vanished years ago, and now a pearl arrives in the post every year. Sherlock Holmes and Dr Watson follow a trail of footprints, a clever little dog and a boat on the Thames to a treasure that men have killed for.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: Twelve cases, told by Dr Watson: a king in a mask, a club for red-haired men, a goose with a jewel inside, a deadly snake in a locked room. Sherlock Holmes reads the smallest clues and solves each puzzle with wit, courage and a little mercy.

title: The Moonstone
author: Wilkie Collins
blurb: A sacred yellow diamond is a birthday gift, and by morning it has vanished from a locked cabinet. As a famous detective, a faithful steward and three silent watchers hunt for it, the truth proves stranger, and closer to home, than anyone guessed.

title: The Woman in White
author: Wilkie Collins
blurb: A pale woman in white appears on a moonlit road and asks Walter Hartright for help. Soon he is caught in a plot of stolen names, with a charming villain who keeps pet mice. Can he save the woman he loves?

title: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
author: Edgar Allan Poe
blurb: Two women are found dead in a locked room in Paris, and the police are baffled. Only Auguste Dupin, a strange night-owl with a brilliant mind, can follow the clues, from a hidden window spring to a shrill voice that nobody understands.

title: The Innocence of Father Brown
author: G. K. Chesterton
blurb: A small, shabby priest with a round face and an umbrella understands crime better than any detective. In six famous tales, Father Brown outwits the master thief Flambeau, solves an impossible murder and uncovers a hero's dark secret.

title: The Mystery of the Yellow Room
author: Gaston Leroux
blurb: A young woman is attacked in a locked room with barred windows, yet the attacker has vanished. Eighteen-year-old reporter Rouletabille follows clues from a muddy lake to a long gallery, and finds a truth stranger than any ghost.

title: Arsène Lupin, Gentleman-Burglar
author: Maurice Leblanc
blurb: Arsène Lupin robs the rich, outwits the police and always keeps his word. Nine daring adventures take him from a stormy ocean liner to a prison cell, a castle with a secret passage, and a meeting with Sherlock Holmes.

title: The Thirty-Nine Steps
author: John Buchan
blurb: London, May 1914. Richard Hannay is bored until a frightened neighbour tells him of a plot, and is then found dead. Hunted by police and spies, Hannay runs for the Scottish hills with a coded notebook. Can he decode it before it is too late?

title: Eight Guests, One Storm
author: And Then There Were None
blurb: Eight guests cross a tidal causeway to Tern Rock Lodge for a weekend of goodbyes. Then the storm shuts the sea road, the lights go out, and the host is dead at the bottom of the cellar steps. Ines Calloway must find the killer before the tide turns.

title: The Counselor's Last Session
author: The Silent Patient
blurb: On her last day as a counselor, Marianne Cole hears one client finally speak about the night his sister died. Then he hands her a key and vanishes. Bound by her promise to keep secrets, she must decide how far to go to save him.

title: The Wife Who Vanished
author: Gone Girl
blurb: On the eve of the Lantern Festival, Isla Marlowe disappears from her clock workshop. Her husband is blamed, but her sister Hannah finds a stopped clock, a brass key and a game from childhood. Where has Isla gone, and who wants her silent?

title: Murder at Maple Court
author: The Thursday Murder Club
blurb: At Maple Court, four retired friends meet every Wednesday over cake to solve old crimes. When the owner who wanted to sell their beloved garden is found dead in the glasshouse, they get a real mystery, with a locked door and a lie about a train.

title: The Cipher Beneath the Bridge
author: The Da Vinci Code
blurb: An engineer is hired to condemn a Victorian iron bridge, but beneath it she finds twelve plates of strange letters. With a shy archivist she follows a cipher from the river to a mill and a bell. Someone close to them is whispering to the man who wants the bridge gone.

title: The Hacker With the Red Scarf
author: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
blurb: Tamsin Rook breaks into computers for a living, always with permission, and always in her grandmother's red scarf. When a kind treasurer is blamed for stolen charity money, she must find the real thief. Every clue is fair. Can you spot him first?

title: Neighbours Who Know Too Much
author: Big Little Lies
blurb: Priya Nair moves into a quiet seaside street where one old man writes down everything his neighbours do. After the Midsummer party, he is found dead. Everyone had a secret, and everyone had a lantern. Who knew too much?

title: The Housekeeper's Notebook
author: The Maid
blurb: Ada Brennan has kept house at Fenwick House for thirty years and written down every small thing she noticed. When her employer dies after his birthday dinner, the police look at her first. Her green notebook may be the only proof she has.

title: Window Seat, Platform Nine
author: The Girl on the Train
blurb: Every morning the 7:42 stops for one minute beside a garden, and a woman in a yellow coat waves. Then she vanishes, and only Mina, a jobless bookkeeper with a window seat and a sharp eye, believes something is wrong.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
blurb: A storm sweeps a Kansas girl and her little dog into a strange, bright land. To get home, Dorothy must follow a yellow road to the Emerald City, with three odd friends who each long for something they already have.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: An inventor builds a machine that can travel through time, then returns pale, bruised and silent. His story takes us to the year 802,701, where gentle people play in the sun and something terrible waits underground. What happened to the world we know?

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: One quiet summer night, a shooting star falls on a common outside London. Soon giant machines are marching across England, burning everything in their path. A writer survives the invasion from Mars, and learns what really saved the Earth.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
blurb: A young scientist discovers the secret of life and builds a living being, then runs from it in horror. Abandoned and alone, the Creature comes looking for the one who made him. Mary Shelley's great story asks who the real monster is.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
blurb: A young lawyer travels to a lonely castle in the mountains to meet a polite and very strange Count. Soon the Count follows him to England, and a small band of friends must stop an ancient evil before it takes everyone they love.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
blurb: In 1866 a mysterious sea monster is sinking ships, and a French professor sails out to hunt it. What he finds is far stranger: Captain Nemo and his wonderful underwater ship. Now the professor is a guest who may never go home.

title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
blurb: Hunger solves a secret: a coded note leads Professor Lidenbrock, his nephew Axel and a silent Icelandic guide down a volcano into a hidden sea of monsters and storms. Jules Verne's classic adventure takes them to the edge of the Earth.

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
blurb: A shy Mole leaves his spring cleaning and finds the river, a loyal Rat and a vain, car-mad Toad. Through snowy woods, a night of strange music and a battle for Toad Hall, four friends learn what home and friendship are worth.

title: The Jungle Book
author: Rudyard Kipling
blurb: A boy raised by wolves, a bear who teaches the Law, a panther who loves him and a tiger who wants him. Follow Mowgli, brave little Rikki-Tikki-Tavi and a boy called Toomai through Kipling's jungle. Can the man-cub find where he belongs?

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
blurb: In foggy London, a quiet lawyer follows a trail of strange clues to a cruel little man called Hyde, and to the secret of his old friend Dr Jekyll. A classic tale of good, evil and the dark side we hide.

title: The Academy Under the Mountain
author: Harry Potter
blurb: Wren Tallow can hear the hum inside every lamp, and it is her ticket to a secret school carved inside a mountain. But the mountain's great heart is growing quiet, and only a new student who listens closely can find out why.

title: The Last Lantern of Aldermoor
author: The Lord of the Rings
blurb: A grey fog is spreading across Aldermoor, and everyone it touches forgets who they are. Corin, a ferryman's son, is handed the last burning lantern and must carry it across marsh, forest, mountain and sea before its light goes out.

title: The Reluctant Burglar's Map
author: The Hobbit
blurb: Ilse Quill mends maps and never leaves home after dark. Then a sea captain asks her to read a thief's old chart and steal the one map that could feed a hungry island. Ilse would much rather stay and drink her tea.

title: Crowns of Salt and Ash
author: A Game of Thrones
blurb: When King Edric dies, his will names no heir, only a test. His clever youngest daughter Sera sees that someone is forging letters to push the Salt Coast and the Ash Hills into war. Can a quiet reader of old books keep two crowns at peace?

title: The Water Merchant's Daughter
author: Dune
blurb: In the desert city of Oshenar every drop of water is counted. When the Deep Well starts to fall and her father vanishes, young Ysra Vell crosses the Glass Desert with a wind-reader to find out who is stealing the city's river.

title: Arena of Dust
author: The Hunger Games
blurb: Every year, one young person from each dry settlement is sent into the Bowl, a desert arena built by the Governor. Ilka can find water where no one else can. In the Bowl, she finds a secret that could change everything.

title: The Boy Who Won the Simulation
author: Ender's Game
blurb: Twelve-year-old Kofi is brilliant at a tide game, so the Tide Academy invites him to train on its great Simulation. He works, learns and wins every test. Then comes the final exam, and nothing about it is what he believes.

title: Survival Log, Day One
author: The Martian
blurb: A flare, a missed lift-off and a note on a whiteboard: everyone thinks Joon-ho is gone. He is alone at the Moon's south pole with a broken radio, a faulty air filter and one clear plan, which is to stay alive.

title: The Signal From Tau Lyra
author: Project Hail Mary
blurb: On a lonely night shift in the Chilean desert, a radio astronomer hears a pattern in the static. It is a message from a faraway star, and it is a call for help. Can one small team answer in time?

title: Neon Rain City
author: Neuromancer
blurb: In a city that never stops raining, an old data thief mends umbrellas and tries to forget her past. Then a child brings her a glass key, and a company's secret plan to let the sea drown a poor district. One last job remains.

title: A Traveller's Guide to Nowhere
author: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
blurb: Oswin Pargeter is the most careful man in Bristol, until a rude and wonderful guidebook arrives on his doormat with a holiday he never booked. Now he must cross a very silly galaxy to find a stamp and a way home.

title: One Small Step a Day
author: Atomic Habits
blurb: Big plans fade, but tiny steps stay. Follow Priya as she swaps heroic resolutions for actions so small they feel almost silly, and see how a few quiet minutes a day can change your reading, your health and your life.

title: Focus Without the Noise
author: Deep Work
blurb: Your phone buzzes, your inbox grows, and your mind will not settle. Follow Noor, a busy translator, as she learns to protect her attention, one calm block of time at a time, and finally finishes the work that matters most.

title: Do Less, Do It Well
author: Essentialism
blurb: Lena says yes to everything, and she is worn out. With help from Rosa, who runs a tiny restaurant with a short menu, she learns to choose what matters, say no kindly, and do fewer things with real care.

title: Hard Task First
author: Eat That Frog
blurb: Every day holds one job you keep dodging, and it is usually the one that matters most. Follow Noor, Lucia and Jonas as they learn to do the hardest task first, in small, kind and practical steps.

title: A Clear Head, A Clear Day
author: Getting Things Done
blurb: Your mind is brilliant at thinking and hopeless at storing. Follow Amara and Dev as they empty their heads onto paper, sort what they find and learn to trust a simple system, so that every day starts clear.

title: Your First Hour
author: The Miracle Morning
blurb: How you spend your first hour can set the tone of the whole day. Follow Mei, Kofi and Elena as they build a short, kind and realistic morning routine, without hype, from the night before to a calm first step.

title: The Learning Mind
author: Mindset
blurb: Maya buys an old guitar and believes she has no talent for it. Over one year she learns how the brain changes with practice, why mistakes help, and how to keep growing at anything, from music to work.

title: Keep Going
author: Grit
blurb: Ben decides to build a wooden rowing boat in his garage, a job that will take two years. Follow him through the excitement, the dull middle, the mistakes and the doubters, and learn how people keep going until the work is done.

title: Stronger Than You Think
author: Can't Hurt Me
blurb: When Dara loses her job, she feels she has nothing left. One small hard thing at a time, from a morning walk to a ten-kilometre race, she finds how much strength was there all along, and how you can build more.

title: Decide Your Direction
author: Awaken the Giant Within
blurb: Leon has drifted for years, until his aunt Rosa, a ferry captain, shows him that every day is full of small decisions. Follow one year of choosing a direction, taking a first step, and steering through setbacks.

title: Goals That Stick
author: Think and Grow Rich
blurb: Kofi has wished for years to make pottery, and nothing has happened. With help from Ana, a retired mountain guide, he turns a wish into a goal with a date, a plan and a price. Follow six months of real progress, slumps and all.

title: Here and Now
author: The Power of Now
blurb: Elise is always thinking about tomorrow, until she misses her stop and finds a garden and an old gardener named Yusuf. Over one season of digging, breathing and noticing, she learns simple ways to come back to the present moment.

title: Choose What Matters
author: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
blurb: You only have so much attention, and everything you care about uses some of it. This short, honest guide shows how to stop caring about everything, choose the few things worth your struggle, and spend your days on purpose.

title: Purpose in Hard Times
author: Man's Search for Meaning
blurb: When life turns painful, big goals can feel impossible. Follow Ruth, Omar and Lena through a job loss, a flood and a long illness at home, and learn small, honest ways to keep a purpose alive when everything is hard.

title: A Reason to Get Up
author: Ikigai
blurb: Some mornings, the alarm is not enough. Meet Grace, a retired teacher, and Kofi, who works nights, as they find small, real reasons to start the day, and learn how you can find yours too.

title: Four Simple Rules for Life
author: The Four Agreements
blurb: Leo is tired, tangled and overpromising. His neighbour Ada, a retired ferry captain, hands him four plain white cards. Follow him through a year of small changes, and see how four simple rules can steady an ordinary life.

title: Quiet Confidence
author: Ego Is the Enemy
blurb: Sam has just been promoted, and he is determined to look brilliant. Helen, a retired stage manager, shows him another way. Learn what quiet confidence is, how it grows, and why people who do not need to impress anyone often do the best work.

title: Free From Other People's Opinions
author: The Courage to Be Disliked
blurb: Lina says yes to everyone and no to herself. Her aunt Rosa, a tailor, teaches her an old idea: what people think of you is their business, and what you do is yours. Join Lina as she learns to be kind, honest and free.

title: How to Get Along With Anyone
author: How to Win Friends and Influence People
blurb: Nora has a new job, a grumpy baker and a big wish to be liked. Over one year she learns the small, practical skills of listening, kindness, honest talk and calm disagreement. They will help you get along with almost anyone.

title: Live by Your Principles
author: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
blurb: Ines runs a small bike shop and feels she is always rushing, never steering. With her grandfather's old brass compass on the wall, she learns to find what matters most and make daily choices that match it. A practical year of steady, honest living.

title: Worry Less, Live More
author: How to Stop Worrying and Start Living
blurb: Elif lies awake at night with a head full of what-ifs. Over one growing season, her neighbour Mrs Hale teaches her, among the vegetable beds, how to ask better questions, take small steps and let go of what cannot be controlled. Calm, practical and kind.

title: As a Man Thinketh
author: James Allen
blurb: A hundred-year-old little book with one big idea: your thoughts are seeds, and your life is the garden that grows from them. James Allen shows how the mind shapes character, health, goals and peace.

title: The Science of Getting Rich
author: Wallace D. Wattles
blurb: In 1910 Wallace Wattles promised a method for getting rich: think clearly, act today and give more than you take. Read his famous ideas page by page, with honest notes on what is belief, what is advice and what is worth keeping.

title: Acres of Diamonds
author: Russell H. Conwell
blurb: A farmer sells his land to hunt for diamonds far away, while a fortune lies under his own garden. Russell Conwell's famous talk asks where your opportunities are hiding. Read the tale, the advice and honest notes on what still holds true today.

title: The Way to Wealth
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: At a crowded sale, old Father Abraham answers a worried crowd with the sayings of Poor Richard: work hard, spend wisely and never run into debt. Benjamin Franklin's famous speech is funny, sharp and surprisingly modern.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
blurb: An ancient Chinese book of strategy, retold in fifty short steps. Sun Tzu argues that the best victory is the one won without a fight, through planning, patience, timing and knowing yourself and your rival. Its ideas still work today.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
blurb: A short, famous and shocking handbook of power, written in 1513 by an unemployed Florentine official. Machiavelli asks how rulers win a state, keep it and lose it. Read it in fifty steps and decide for yourself whether it is honest advice, a warning, or both.

title: Your Money, Your Rules
author: Rich Dad Poor Dad and The Psychology of Money
blurb: Priya has just received her first full pay, and her neighbour has a year of simple ideas to share. Learn to plan, save, borrow wisely and invest with patience, then write rules that fit your own life.

title: Assets and Liabilities in Plain Words
author: Rich Dad Poor Dad
blurb: Leila's money disappears every month and she cannot say why. Over tea, a retired shopkeeper gives her one simple question that sorts everything she owns or owes into assets and liabilities, and then shows her what to do next.

title: How Money Really Works
author: The Psychology of Money and The Intelligent Investor
blurb: Ana and Ben start work on the same day, on the same pay. Ten years later their money tells two very different stories. Find out why saving, patience, luck and fear matter more than clever tricks, and how money really works.

title: Start Investing Today
author: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
blurb: Mira has some savings and no idea where to start. With the help of her cousin Dev, she learns what shares, bonds and index funds are, why costs matter, and how a simple plan can carry an ordinary person through good years and bad.

title: The Index Fund Way
author: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
blurb: Leila has saved some money for the first time, and everyone has advice. Follow her as she learns, step by step, why a plain, low-cost index fund may beat clever tricks, and how patience does the real work.

title: Small Savings, Big Future
author: The Millionaire Next Door
blurb: Amara and Joel earn a fair wage, yet each month their money seems to vanish. With help from wise Aunt Wen, they learn small, steady habits that turn spare coins into freedom. Real people, real choices, and a future that grows quietly.

title: One Simple Plan for Wealth
author: The Simple Path to Wealth
blurb: Marta delivers parcels, worries about money, and has no plan. Over ten years she builds one on a single page: know your numbers, keep a gap, clear debt, hold a cushion, and let one plain fund grow. Simple enough to start tonight.

title: Build It Lean
author: The Lean Startup
blurb: Mira has an idea that she is sure the whole street will love. Before she spends a year and all her savings on it, she learns how to test it with small, cheap experiments. A clear, practical guide to starting new things wisely.

title: Build Something New
author: Zero to One
blurb: Ravi watches good vegetables rot in the heat of the market and wonders why nobody has fixed it. This is the story of how he sets out to make something truly new, and a plain guide to choosing, starting and protecting an idea that matters.

title: How Strong Companies Last
author: Good to Great
blurb: Brightwell Paper has survived seventy years while louder, richer rivals disappeared. A young manager asks its retired boss why. Over fifty Friday conversations she learns what quietly separates companies that last from those that only shine for a while.

title: Lead Through the Hard Days
author: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
blurb: Kofi runs a small delivery company, and in one week a third of his income walks out the door. Follow his hard year, with a retired manager at his side, and learn how to tell the truth, decide, and care for people when things go wrong.

title: Work Less, Earn Smart
author: The 4-Hour Workweek
blurb: Leo works sixty hours a week and still feels behind. Over one year, with help from a friend who runs a workshop, he learns to measure results instead of hours, say no, raise his prices and build a calmer way to earn a living.

title: Lead With Purpose
author: Start With Why
blurb: Sofia's bakery is busy, but she cannot say why it exists, and a cheaper rival is stealing her customers. With an old sea captain as her guide, she learns what purpose really is, how to find it, and how to lead people by it.

title: Negotiate Without Fighting
author: Never Split the Difference
blurb: You negotiate every day: with a boss, a landlord, a shop, a sister. This short guide shows how to listen, ask, stay calm and still get a good deal, without raising your voice or losing the person across the table.

title: Why People Buy
author: Influence
blurb: Why does one person buy and another walk away? Follow Rosa, who runs a small bakery, as she learns what really moves people: feelings, trust, fear of risk and the power of a good story, and how to be persuasive without ever being unfair.

title: Teach Yourself to Be Wealthy
author: I Will Teach You to Be Rich
blurb: Nina has just started her first job and has no idea what to do with her pay. Learn with her how to plan your spending, clear debts, build savings and start investing, in simple steps that anyone can follow and no special talent.

title: The Dhammapada
author: Buddhist scripture (traditional)
blurb: Four hundred and twenty-three short verses, said to carry the voice of the Buddha, on the mind, anger, happiness and freedom. Walk through the best-loved of them, chapter by chapter, and see why they have been read for more than two thousand years.

title: Tao Te Ching
author: Laozi
blurb: Eighty-one tiny chapters, written in ancient China and said to come from a sage named Laozi. They speak of water, silence, softness and simple living. Read the best-loved of them, and see why this small book has been translated into hundreds of languages.

title: The Bhagavad Gita
author: Hindu scripture (traditional)
blurb: On a battlefield, a prince sits down in despair, and his charioteer begins to speak. In 700 verses, the most loved scripture of India asks what we owe to others, what we really are, and how to act well without fear. Read the conversation chapter by chapter.

title: The Sermon on the Mount
author: Gospel of Matthew
blurb: On a hillside above the Sea of Galilee, Jesus sits down and teaches the crowds. Follow the Sermon on the Mount from the Beatitudes to the wise builder, and hear some of the most famous words ever spoken about kindness, honesty and trust.

title: The Book of Proverbs
author: Hebrew Bible
blurb: Short, sharp sayings about money, friends, words, work and the good life, gathered in ancient Israel and still quoted today. Walk through the Book of Proverbs, from a father's advice to a son to the poem of the capable woman.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
blurb: A Roman emperor writes in his army tent at night, not for the world but for himself. Meditations gathers the private reminders of Marcus Aurelius on anger, duty, time, death and kindness, ideas that readers have kept close for nearly two thousand years.

title: The Prophet
author: Kahlil Gibran
blurb: A wise stranger has waited twelve years in the city of Orphalese for his ship. Before he sails, the people ask him about love, work, joy, pain, freedom and death. His answers, in the poetry of Kahlil Gibran, have comforted readers for a hundred years.

title: The Analects of Confucius
author: Confucius
blurb: Two and a half thousand years ago a teacher in China spoke simply about learning, kindness, honesty and how to live well. His students wrote his words down. Meet Confucius through the sayings and small stories of the Analects.

title: The Enchiridion
author: Epictetus
blurb: A man born into slavery became one of the great teachers of ancient Greece and Rome. His handbook says that we cannot control the world, only how we meet it. Fifty short lessons on calm, courage and freedom, still fresh nearly two thousand years later.

title: Be Here, Be Calm
author: Wherever You Go, There You Are
blurb: Maya is always rushing, always somewhere else in her head. Over six weeks of small, honest practice, she learns to arrive in her own life, one breath at a time. A calm, practical guide to being here.

title: The Mind That Watches
author: The Untethered Soul
blurb: Ines cannot stop worrying, so she takes a summer job at a tiny railway station. There, an old stationmaster teaches her to sit on the platform and watch her thoughts arrive and leave like trains. A gentle book about the part of you that notices.

title: Walk Slowly, Breathe Deeply
author: The Miracle of Mindfulness
blurb: Hana has just retired and cannot stop hurrying, even with nowhere to go. A quiet neighbour shows her how to walk slowly beside the river, and how to breathe as if each breath were new. A gentle guide to walking and breathing.

title: Staying Calm When Life Breaks
author: When Things Fall Apart
blurb: One grey Tuesday Noor loses her job, and by night her father is in hospital. Follow her through a few hard weeks as an old ferry captain teaches her calm: simple steps, drawn from many traditions, for when life breaks.

title: Radical Kindness to Yourself
author: Radical Acceptance
blurb: Elena makes one small mistake at work, and the voice in her head turns cruel. Join a quiet Thursday circle in a library and learn, step by step, how to be on your own side: warm, practical and wise.

title: What Joy Really Is
author: The Book of Joy
blurb: On his thirty-fifth birthday, teacher Ravi has everything he wanted and feels nothing. So he takes a month of trains to ask bakers, nuns, singers and gardeners what joy really is, and how to let it in.

title: A Purpose Bigger Than You
author: The Purpose Driven Life
blurb: What is your life for? Walk with a baker, a bus driver, a cleaner, a retired engineer and a teenager as they discover that purpose grows when it reaches beyond yourself. Small, practical steps for anyone, with or without faith.

title: Life as a Seeker
author: Autobiography of a Yogi
blurb: Ines grows up asking questions on a harbour wall, then sets out to find answers. She sits in silence with monks and meditators, shares music, bread and long roads with strangers, and learns that seeking is a way of living, not a place to arrive.

title: The Last Lessons of a Teacher
author: Tuesdays with Morrie
blurb: When her old schoolteacher writes that she is dying, busy Priya begins to visit her every Saturday morning. Over tea beneath a pear tree, Miss Brandt gives her last lessons on attention, apology, joy, letting go and how to live well.

title: Letting Go of the Ego
author: A New Earth
blurb: Leila wins every argument and still feels empty. Over one summer at an old harbour boatyard, a retired boat builder teaches her to notice the proud, defensive voice inside her, and to hold it more lightly.

title: Stillness for Beginners
author: Be Here Now
blurb: Seventeen-year-old Eli spends four winter weeks on his grandmother's farm, where nobody hurries and nothing buzzes. She teaches him the plainest skill there is: how to sit still, and what turns up when you do.

title: Forgiveness, Step by Step
author: The Book of Forgiving
blurb: Three years ago Nell's brother sold their late father's café without telling her, and she has not spoken to him since. Over one spring, a retired teacher walks beside her through the slow, honest steps of forgiveness.

title: A Calm and Happy Life
author: The Art of Happiness
blurb: Is a calm and happy life possible for ordinary people? This short book of simple ideas, shared by many wisdom traditions, shows small practices you can try today, one calm step at a time.

title: Walking
author: Henry David Thoreau
blurb: Why does a person need to wander outdoors with no goal at all? Thoreau's famous essay answers with swamps, sunsets and a daily saunter of four hours. Walk through his ideas and find a calmer, wilder way to spend an afternoon.

title: Eat More Plants
author: How Not to Die
blurb: Lena is tired of ready meals, and her neighbour is a retired dietitian. Follow one year in their kitchens and gardens as they learn what plants do for the body, and how to enjoy a lot more of them, one simple meal at a time.

title: The Long Life Plan
author: Outlive
blurb: Omar is fifty-two and wants more than a long life: he wants a good one. Over a year of walks up Bell Hill, his sister Salma shows him what really helps people stay strong, sharp and independent, and what is only hype.

title: Hormones and Hunger, Explained
author: The Obesity Code
blurb: Noor is a baker who is always hungry by four o'clock, and her neighbour Ines is a retired nurse. Together they follow the body's hunger signals, from the stomach to the brain, and learn what science knows and what it does not.

title: Sleep Is Your Superpower
author: Why We Sleep
blurb: Lena has an exam in two weeks and has been studying until three every morning. Her aunt Rosa, who works in a sleep clinic, shows her what really happens in the brain at night, and why sleep may be the best study tool she has.

title: Breathe Better, Feel Better
author: Breath
blurb: Iris sings in a choir, and her breath races before every concert. Her friend Dev, a lung physiotherapist, takes her on a tour of the nose, the lungs and the diaphragm, and shows what slow, steady breathing can and cannot do.

title: Run Like a Kid Again
author: Born to Run
blurb: Sam is forty-two and loses his breath chasing a football. His eight-year-old daughter runs for pure joy, so he decides to learn again, one gentle step at a time, from a first slow jog to a first five-kilometre run.

title: Exercise for a Sharper Mind
author: Spark
blurb: Leila keeps losing her keys and her words, and she spends all day at a desk. When her nephew Ravi, who studies the brain, comes to stay, he takes her out walking and explains what movement may really do for memory, focus and mood.

title: Where People Live Longest
author: The Blue Zones
blurb: Elena is a data analyst, and her grandmother Nina is about to turn ninety. Before the birthday party, the two of them study maps, charts and daily habits to find out why people in some places live longer than others, and what is luck, what is place and what is choice.

title: Foods That Protect You
author: Eat to Beat Disease
blurb: Amara has to design a science project about food, and her grandfather Kofi used to be a cook. Together they sort the real evidence from the hype about which foods help the body look after itself.

title: Feed Your Gut
author: Fiber Fueled
blurb: Noah rides a bicycle for a living and wants to feel lighter and stronger. His neighbour Ines studies microbes, and she shows him the tiny world inside every gut, and how everyday food can help it thrive.

title: Steady Energy All Day
author: Good Energy
blurb: By three o'clock every afternoon, Hana's energy has vanished. Her colleague Dev, a running coach, helps her test what really gives steady energy: sleep, light, meals, movement and stress, with the evidence for each.

title: Why Healthy Food Feels So Hard
author: The Hungry Brain
blurb: Noor wants to eat well, yet every evening her appetite wins. With her uncle Idris, a retired dietitian, she learns why: old hunger signals, clever food, tired evenings and busy lives. Then she finds small, kind changes that really work.

title: Lift Heavy, Start Simple
author: Starting Strength
blurb: Kofi is forty-four, sits all day and is out of breath on the stairs. With Ana, a patient coach, he learns to squat, hinge, push, pull and carry, then adds weight a little at a time. A simple start for anyone who has never lifted.

title: Ten Moves for a Lifetime
author: Built to Move
blurb: After a small stumble on the pavement, Grace, sixty-three, wants to stay strong and independent for life. Her neighbour Mateo, a physiotherapist, teaches her ten simple everyday moves, from walking to getting up off the floor, and how to practise each one safely.

title: The Stress Reset
author: Why Zebras Don't Get Ulcers
blurb: Why does stress make your heart race, your shoulders ache and your sleep go wrong? Follow a tired teacher through one stressful week and learn what stress really does to the body, then try simple, proven ways to switch the alarm off.

title: A Better Night, Starting Tonight
author: The Sleep Revolution
blurb: Lena can't sleep, and tomorrow is a big day. Follow her as she learns how sleep really works, why it goes wrong, and which small changes you can make tonight to wake up feeling like yourself again.

title: Why Moving Makes You Happy
author: The Joy of Movement
blurb: Priya sits at a desk all day and feels flat. A fifteen-minute walk changes her afternoon, and she wants to know why. Discover what movement does to your mood, mind and body, and how to begin, even if you hate exercise.

title: Stay Strong Past Fifty
author: Younger Next Year
blurb: Marta is fifty-seven when she cannot rise from the lawn without help. With her neighbour Sam, a physiotherapist, she learns how muscles, bones, balance and friends can stay strong for decades, one small step at a time.

title: Twelve Rules for a Sharper Brain
author: Brain Rules
blurb: Teo, forty-six, keeps forgetting names and where he put his keys. His friend Ada, a psychology teacher, gives him twelve rules about sleep, attention, memory and calm. Each one is simple, backed by real research and easy to try this week.

title: Real Food, Simple Rules
author: In Defense of Food
blurb: Elif eats takeaway, ready meals and desk snacks, and every headline tells her something different. Her uncle Davit, a cook for forty years, gives her simple rules for shopping, cooking and eating well, with no diet and no guilt.

title: The Histories
author: Herodotus
blurb: Kings who trust the wrong oracle, a baby saved from a murderous order, a bridge of boats and three hundred Spartans in a narrow pass. Herodotus, the first historian, tells how the Greeks and the Persians came to war, and who won.

title: The Gallic War
author: Julius Caesar
blurb: A general writes his own war report. Julius Caesar tells how he led Roman legions across Gaul, bridged the Rhine, sailed to Britain and faced the brilliant Vercingetorix at Alesia. Eight years of battle, as the winner chose to tell it.

title: Plutarch's Lives
author: Plutarch
blurb: A boy who lifts a rock, a general who cuts a knot, a queen who sails in on a golden barge. Plutarch, the great biographer, tells the lives of famous Greeks and Romans, and shows how small moments reveal a person's character.

title: The Travels of Marco Polo
author: Marco Polo
blurb: A teenage merchant from Venice rides with his father and uncle across deserts, mountains and seas to the court of Kublai Khan. Marco Polo stayed for seventeen years, then came home with stories so wonderful that many people refused to believe them.

title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Born into slavery in Maryland, Frederick Douglass was never told his birthday and was forbidden to read. This is his own true story of how he taught himself, stood up to a cruel master and escaped to freedom, told in his own brave words.

title: Up From Slavery
author: Booker T. Washington
blurb: Born a slave in Virginia, Booker Washington walked and begged his way to school, swept a classroom to prove himself, and later built a famous college from nothing. Here is his own honest, hopeful story of work, learning and courage.

title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: Benjamin Franklin was a poor Boston printer's apprentice who ran away at seventeen with almost no money. In his own warm, funny, honest words, he tells how he taught himself, built a business and a city, and tried to become a better man.

title: Twelve Years a Slave
author: Solomon Northup
blurb: Solomon Northup was a free Black man, a husband, a father and a fine violin player, living in New York. In 1841 two strangers tricked him, and he woke in chains. This is his true story of twelve years of bondage, and of the day he was found.

title: How Humans Took Over the World
author: Sapiens
blurb: We are not the strongest animal, or the fastest, or the oldest. So how did one species from Africa end up filling every continent, building cities and walking on the Moon? Follow the whole story, from the first stone tool to the world of eight billion.

title: Why Some Countries Got Rich First
author: Guns, Germs, and Steel
blurb: Why do some countries have so much and others so little? Follow the long story from the first farms to the first factories, and weigh the answers that historians offer: place, rules and sheer chance.

title: The Roads That Built the World
author: The Silk Roads
blurb: From a line of footprints in volcanic ash to cables on the sea floor, follow the roads, rivers and sea lanes that carried silk, spices, gold, ideas and sometimes disease, and see how they joined the world together.

title: Rome in Ten Moments
author: SPQR
blurb: Ten turning points, from a legend about twins and a wolf to the day the last western emperor was sent away. Walk through a thousand years of Rome, five steps at a time, and see why this one city still matters.

title: The Horseback Empire
author: Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World
blurb: In 1206 a poor, abandoned boy from the grasslands was named Genghis Khan. Within a lifetime, his riders and their heirs ruled lands from the Pacific to Poland. This is how it happened, what it cost, and why it still matters.

title: The Americas Before Columbus
blurb: Before Columbus, millions of people farmed, built cities and shaped whole landscapes across two continents. Meet the Maya, the Inca, the Aztecs and many others, and learn how their world rose, flourished and was changed for ever.

title: The Salt Trade That Shaped Nations
author: Salt: A World History
blurb: It seasons your dinner, yet salt once paid armies, built roads and sparked revolts. Follow the white crystals from ancient seas to desert caravans, from Roman roads to Gandhi's famous march, and discover how a pinch of salt changed the world.

title: Thirty Days to World War
author: The Guns of August
blurb: A murder in Sarajevo, a promise from Berlin and a deadline for Serbia: follow the thirty days in 1914 when ministers, kings and generals, mostly not wanting war, took step after step into one. A clear story of how Europe slipped.

title: The Rules History Keeps Repeating
author: The Lessons of History
blurb: History never repeats exactly, yet it keeps rhyming. Meet twelve patterns, from stretched empires to bursting bubbles, each shown through real people in Rome, Amsterdam, Paris and beyond. Learn what the past can and cannot tell us.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: In 1859 Charles Darwin published one long argument: living things change over time, and nature itself, not a breeder's hand, picks which ones survive. Follow his book chapter by chapter, from pigeons to fossils to a tangled bank.

title: The Voyage of the Beagle
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: In December 1831 a young Charles Darwin sailed from England on a small survey ship and did not come home for almost five years. Travel with him through jungle, ice, earthquake and volcanic islands, and watch a great idea begin.

title: The Chemical History of a Candle
author: Michael Faraday
blurb: In a lecture hall in London, Michael Faraday lit one ordinary candle and used it to explain fire, air, water and even breathing. Sit among his young audience and see how much a small flame can teach you.

title: Relativity: The Special and General Theory
author: Albert Einstein
blurb: What if two people could disagree about when something happened, and both be right? Einstein's own little book takes you from a train and a lightning bolt to bent starlight and a curved universe, one clear step at a time.

title: Experiments on Plant Hybridisation
author: Gregor Mendel
blurb: In a monastery garden, a monk grew thousands of pea plants, counted every seed and found a hidden law of life. Follow Gregor Mendel's own paper, one clear experiment at a time, from the first cross to the birth of genetics.

title: The Story of Everything, Short
author: A Brief History of Time
blurb: Sit on a dark hilltop and look up. In fifty short steps, this book takes you from the light of the nearest star to the first moments of the universe, and on to the far future, saying clearly what we know and what we still do not.

title: A Tour of the Universe
author: Cosmos
blurb: On a quiet rooftop at night, Noor invites Kit into the Skylift, an imaginary lift that climbs past the Moon, the planets and the stars. Fifty stops later you will have seen the whole universe, as far as anyone has.

title: Why Genes Behave Like They Do
author: The Selfish Gene
blurb: In her grandmother's bakery, Maya finds a box of old recipe cards, and her uncle Teo shows her that every living thing has one too. Fifty short steps explain what genes are, why they get copied, and what they cannot tell us.

title: The Universe in an Afternoon
author: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
blurb: One hot Sunday, Anya asks her uncle Ravi what the universe really is. He promises to tell her before the tea goes cold. Five hours, a chalkboard and fifty short explanations later, she will know what we have learned, and what nobody knows yet.

title: Everything You Missed in School
author: A Short History of Nearly Everything
blurb: Nobody has time to teach you everything. This book takes you from the Big Bang to your own brain in fifty short steps, covering the stars, the Earth, life, atoms and the way science works, and it never talks down to you.

title: Strings, Space and Time
author: The Elegant Universe
blurb: What are space and time made of? Follow two great theories, relativity and quantum physics, to the place where they clash, then meet string theory, a bold and unproven idea about tiny vibrating loops. It is honest about what we know and what we do not.

title: Physics in Six Ideas
author: Six Easy Pieces
blurb: Kofi is twelve and thinks physics is for scientists in white coats. Then his Aunt Zainab, a physics teacher, shows him that one ordinary day on a bike, in a kitchen and under the stars is built on just six big ideas.

title: How Genes Shape Who We Are
author: The Gene
blurb: Why does Noor have her grandmother's curls and her father's green eyes? Over one summer, her aunt Amara, a scientist, shows her the tiny instructions inside every cell, from peas and twins to gene editing, and what they can and cannot tell us.

title: The Fish Inside You
author: Your Inner Fish
blurb: Kofi gets the hiccups in a museum, and a fossil expert tells him that his body is full of old parts. Follow his jaw, his ears, his hands and even his hiccups back through hundreds of millions of years to the first fish.

title: Think Like a Scientist
author: The Demon-Haunted World
blurb: Dev says his lucky socks help his team win, and Ines asks, how would we know? Join their school science club to learn how scientists test ideas, avoid being fooled, and say I might be wrong. A toolkit for thinking, for anyone.

title: Physics, One Idea at a Time
author: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
blurb: Why does a ball fall, a kettle boil, a rainbow shine? Take physics one idea at a time, from motion and energy to atoms, light, bent space and the biggest puzzles nobody has solved. No mathematics needed, only curiosity.

title: Why Time Feels Like It Flows
author: The Order of Time
blurb: You can't touch it, yet it rules your day. Follow time through ancient clocks, Einstein's bent minutes, the arrow that makes eggs break, and the brain that makes an hour fly or crawl, and see why nobody fully understands it.

title: A Tour Through Your Body
author: The Body
blurb: Take a guided tour of the one place you have always lived. From skin and bones to the heart, the brain, the gut and the tiny cells inside, discover how your body works, and why it is stranger and more wonderful than you thought.

title: The Secret World of Fungi
author: Entangled Life
blurb: A mushroom is only the visible tip. Walk through a wet forest and discover the hidden threads beneath it: fungi that recycle the dead, feed the trees, grow in our bread and medicine, and still hold secrets scientists have not yet named.

title: Earth Seen From Space
author: Pale Blue Dot
blurb: Ana is an astronaut with one promise to keep: to describe the whole Earth to her young niece. Through the windows of the space station, you will see storms, rivers, reefs, cities and auroras, and understand why our home looks so small and precious.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
blurb: A wild moor, two haunted houses and a love too fierce for either. Heathcliff, a homeless boy, grows up beside Catherine Earnshaw, and when she chooses another man, his revenge reaches into the next generation. Emily Brontë's masterpiece, retold for learners.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
blurb: Four sisters, one small house and a war far away. Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy grow up in the March family, learning about love, loss and following their dreams. Louisa May Alcott's beloved story of home, retold for learners.

title: The Valley of Fear
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: A coded warning, a body in a moated Sussex house, and a face that is not whose it seems. Holmes unravels a murder at Birlstone, then follows it back to a dark valley in Pennsylvania where a secret society ruled by fear.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: A stranger wrapped in bandages arrives at a quiet inn in a snowstorm, and beneath the wrappings there is nothing at all. When a brilliant scientist's secret is found, a village is thrown into fear, and one old friend must stop him.
